the persistence of a highly parochially focused political outlook, combined with a top-down approach, undermined the participatory governance intentions of devolved government in the context of national park designation in Northern Ireland.
the policy process was dominated by a highly parochially minded political class that sought to undermine attempts to introduce participatory governance in order to protect the status quo.
the persistence of a highly parochal political outlook combined with a top-down approach towards policy-making has undermined attempts to designate the Mournes area as a national park.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extent to which devolved government has provided opportunities for participatory governance in Northern Ireland.
the potential for participatory governance to contribute to democratic renewal in the devolved UK.
how participatory governance is being enacted and how this is being shaped by structural factors in a devolving context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the policy making process was highly centralised, with the political elite having the final say in the designation of the Mournes as a national park.
the process was not participatory.
participatory governance in Northern Ireland is a long way from being realised and, in the case of the Mourne policy development, the potential of participatory governance was not met.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the policy process in the Mourne National Park designation was characterised by an absence of participation, a lack of transparency and a top down approach to consultation.
participatory governance in Northern Ireland has not been fully realised.
the paper reveals how the political context of devolving government has impacted on policy development in the context of a national park.
The main takeaway from our work is that
participatory governance in Northern Ireland remains a work in progress.

the devolution of power to the local level in a context of political and cultural fragmentation is unlikely to be successful without significant reform of the structures of government and the development of a culture of participatory democracy.
participatory policy making in a devolving governance context requires a re-evaluation of power relations and the need for a new political culture to emerge that embraces participatory democracy.
